findings.title: plural network echoed in the rationale
findings.claim: The broken plural awliya names a networked protective role and returns as the predicate of the rationale.
findings.mechanism: Its accusative occurrence assigns the prohibited role, while the same plural in the following nominative verbless clause describes the groups' existing mutual role.
findings.reader_payoff: The rationale is heard as an explanation of the command: their reciprocal network is already in place.
findings.containment: Keeps the ordinary ally and protector sense in view and bounds wider authority nuances to the supplied wording.

epistemic.reason: Trusted word-analysis evidence directly anchors this distinct local relation.

findings.title: prohibited walī role
findings.claim: Awliya covers the prohibited role of ally, protector, patron, or authority-near figure, beyond casual warmth.
findings.mechanism: As the second object of the adoption verb, it names the role assigned to the named groups; the supplied lexical range joins nearness, protection, patronage, and authority.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the warning as a boundary around a chosen protective or governing relation.
findings.containment: Preserves the ordinary social relation while making its authority-near range visible; it does not turn every social contact into the prohibited act.

epistemic.reason: Trusted word-analysis evidence directly anchors this distinct local relation.

findings.mechanism: The same role family is given a positive referent nearby, so the negative command is read as an object-specific boundary.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the command as distinguishing where the protective relation is directed.
findings.containment: This is a supplied local contrast, not a complete account of every later use of the role family.

epistemic.reason: Trusted word-analysis evidence directly anchors this distinct local relation.
